title: Syro-Malabar Malayalam service-book scope reconciliation, 2026-10-20
semantics: Dated reclassification under guidance/time-machine.md §11, clarified 2026-10-19. This note supplements and does not alter the malabar.json research review of 2026-10-19. Candidate status is not an act-history station, a collated textual transition, a complete book, current obligation, or asserted ancestry. Complementary and component books are not successive whole-Taksa editions.

review_files.storage: untracked workspace scratch; proposal pinned here by SHA-256 only

uses.finding: The Church's approved operative Malayalam Qurbana books and complementary/component service books are received service-book-language candidates. The 1962 bilingual book was already a candidate; eleven further IDs move from origin review. The 2005 Propria and 2011 selected-propria Taksa have secondary/contextual Malayalam attribution and are qualified research candidates with original copies uninspected.
uses.limit: No full-book collation, uninterrupted-use interval, direct textual descent, new stage, rights permission, or completed 1968–2025 state sequence follows from this reclassification.

versions.basis: The seven bishops' imprimatur and their decision put the partly Malayalam book into force on 3 July 1962.
versions.limits: The 20 January 1962 instruction promulgated the 1960 Syriac missal, not this Malayalam book. Its separately paginated Syriac section witnesses that restored text; no distinct Syriac revision is claimed without collation.

versions.basis: The bishops' 20 May 1968 imprimatur, reported Roman experimental permission from 15 August, and reported diocesan use establish approval and operation; the later decree describes partial renewal besides translation.
versions.limits: The original 1968 permission instrument and affected passages are unlocated; the order is uncollated with 1962 and the 1974 reimprimatur.

versions.basis: The 19 December 1985 decree approved the most solemn Raza; the Malayalam book carries 8 February 1986 imprimaturs and reports first use at Kottayam that day.
versions.limits: No prayer or rubric collation; the November 1984 and January 1985 texts are study drafts, not this operative book.

versions.basis: Pallath reports decree approval on 3 April 1989 and liturgical use from 3 July; n. 57 names a Malayalam Order of Raza containing the decree.
loci: Pallath 2023 p. 35, English typical edition report
versions.limits: The Malayalam volume and decree have not been directly inspected. The same study also reports an English typical text; its relation to the Malayalam expression and to 1986 remains uncollated.

versions.basis: Pallath reports synodal approval, 10 July recognitio, 1 November decree, effectiveness from 27 November 2005 and four volumes; the commission's retrospective lists the published Propria.
loci: Formation of Syro-Malabar Liturgical Texts, opening context and §2 item 3
versions.limits: Malayalam attribution is secondary/contextual, not an inspected original-language title or text page. Four original volumes and printed decree uninspected; reported new proper items are not collated.

versions.basis: Decree 622/2009 promulgated Christmas and Great Week booklets effective 14 September 2009 and abrogated earlier texts for these rites; a later Christmas printing carries the decree.
versions.limits: The 2009 Great Week booklet is not acquired; the Christmas witness is a 2016/2017 reprint. Neither body is collated.

versions.basis: Pallath reports authorization to select prayers for community use, 2009 synodal approval of 24 selected propria, and publication of a Taksa and people's text in 2011.
loci: Pallath 2023 p. 32, including Synodal News reference n. 62
versions.limits: Malayalam attribution is secondary/contextual; no original 2011 title or text page inspected. Selection and placement are identified, but the 24 prayers are not all claimed as new compositions or a separate whole-Taksa state.

versions.basis: The 2018 reprint prints the 2013 first-print imprimatur and a decree explicitly saying the Church had begun using the Second Qudasha on 15 August 2013.
versions.limits: The 2013 original printing is uninspected. The 2018 definitive decree and reprint do not by themselves prove a distinct textual revision.

versions.basis: Pallath reports synodal approval of three Malayalam proclamation volumes, 10 October 2013 decree and use effective 1 December; the commission lists them as published.
loci: Formation of Syro-Malabar Liturgical Texts §2 item 10
versions.limits: The volumes and decree are not directly inspected. Scripture wording is drawn from the KCBC Malayalam Bible; the Church's appointed reading order is the service-book arrangement.

versions.basis: The Malayalam Third Qudasha booklet prints the 2018 imprimatur, synodal approval, Roman recognitio, decree and 8 September effective date.
versions.limits: The body and relation to earlier anaphora witnesses remain uncollated.

versions.basis: The official book prints recognitio of the Malayalam Raza Taksa as a new editio typica and decree 0775/2021 promulgating the definitive text for Raza, solemn and simple forms effective 28 November 2021.
versions.limits: No independent collation with the 1989 Malayalam book; the 2021 body text layer has legacy-font corruption, and publication rights are unresolved.

versions.basis: Decree 0224/2025 promulgated the revised Malayalam Great Week rites effective 13 April 2025; two presentations contain the same decree.
versions.limits: The two presentations count once. The Christmas text named by the decree is unlocated and the 2009-to-2025 changed passages remain uncollated.

negative_findings: The 1971 solemn booklet has an episcopal imprimatur, but a concrete use or effective-date record has not been identified.
The 1971 sung Requiem is marked experimental, but no issuing authority or imprimatur was identified on the inspected leaves.
The 1974 reimprimatur and 2018 Theodore reprint do not establish separate changed texts. Drafts and unapproved adaptations remain outside the approved-operative candidate set.
The 1868 and 1926 Tukasa ceremonial books have reported authorization or later obligation, but their original books and acts remain uninspected; the 1868 publication reports conflict.
remaining_gap: Acquire and collate the 1989 Malayalam Order, 2005 four-volume Propria, 2011 Taksa, 2013 lectionary and original Theodore printing; establish the original title/language of the 2005 and 2011 books. Acquire earlier Syriac and bilingual books and inspect the Tukasa acts. Determine concrete component changes and relationships before adding book-state stages or act-history stations.
